unmapped: Regret measured against realized return of best fixed arm Gmax (weak regret)
settings.definition_quote: An adversarial bandit problem is specified by the number K of possible actions ... and by an assignment of rewards, i.e., an infinite sequence x(1), x(2), ... of vectors x(t) = (x1(t), ..., xK(t)), where xi(t) ∈ [0, 1] denotes the reward obtained if action i is chosen at time step t. ... We assume that the player knows the number K of actions.

settings.name_in_paper: lower bound on the weak regret (random Bernoulli reward assignment depending on K and T)
unmapped: Instance (good arm and gap epsilon) chosen depending on K and T; good arm chosen uniformly at random
settings.definition_quote: First, before play begins, one action I is chosen uniformly at random to be the "good" action. The T rewards xI(t) associated with the good action are chosen independently at random to be 1 with probability 1/2 + ǫ and 0 otherwise ... The rewards xj(t) associated with the other actions j ≠ I are chosen independently at random to be 0 or 1 with equal odds.

settings.name_in_paper: adversarial bandit problem with N experts
unmapped: Expert advice vectors are probability distributions over K arms; comparator is the expected return of the best expert
settings.definition_quote: Formally, an expert i is an infinite sequence ξi(1), ξi(2), ... ∈ [0,1]^K of probability vectors ... An adversarial bandit problem with N experts is thus specified by both an assignment of rewards to actions and by an assignment of probability vectors to each expert.

settings.name_in_paper: regret against arbitrary sequences of actions (hardness h)
unmapped: Comparator sequence hardness h(j^T) = 1 + number of switches
settings.definition_quote: The hardness of a sequence (j1, ..., jT) is defined by h(j1, ..., jT) = 1 + |{1 ≤ ℓ < T : jℓ ≠ jℓ+1}|.

unmapped: Repeated N-person game; regret is per-round average regret of player i
settings.definition_quote: this corresponds to assuming that the vector (x1(t), ..., xK(t)) of rewards for each trial t is chosen by an adversary who knows the gambler's strategy and the outcome of the gambler's random draws up to time t − 1.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Game-theoretic guarantee: per-round payoff relative to the minimax value of an unknown zero-sum game
unmapped: Entries in known interval [a,b]; guarantee is relative to game value v

source.quote: For any number of actions K ≥ 2 and for any time horizon T, there exists a distribution over the assignment of rewards such that the expected weak regret of any algorithm ... is at least (1/20) min{√(KT), T}.
